CVE-2026-129295.title: mail-parser is vulnerable to polynomial ReDoS in email header parsing
CVE-2026-129295.description: mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 4.2.0 until 4.6.1, attacker-controlled email headers can cause polynomial regular-expression backtracking during ordinary parse_from_string(), parse_from_bytes(), or parse_from_file() calls. In src/mailparser/utils.py, get_addresses() invokes the _ADDR_FALLBACK_RE fallback when strict address parsing yields no usable address, and overlapping quantifiers rescan padded address headers quadratically or cubically. In src/mailparser/const.py, parse_received() applies _CLAUSE_SPLITTER to uncollapsed whitespace in a Received header, causing quadratic backtracking when a whitespace run is not followed by a clause keyword. A small, well-formed message can keep mail gateway, ticketing, quarantine, or archival parsing workers busy for extended periods. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.1.

CVE-2026-99499.title: s390/pci: Fix use-after-free race in zpci floating interrupt cleanup
CVE-2026-99499.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/pci: Fix use-after-free race in zpci floating interrupt cleanup

zpci_clear_irq() stops the adapter from raising new interrupts for the
function, but a zpci_floating_irq_handler() already running on another CPU
can still be scanning zdev->aibv when zpci_msi_teardown_floating() releases
it.

Clear the zpci_ibv[] entry so no further handler picks the vector up, then
wait for a grace period before releasing it. The handler runs inside the
rcu_read_lock() section that do_airq_interrupt() holds across
airq->handler(), so synchronize_rcu() drains any handler still in flight.

arm64: mm: validate /dev/mem mmap ranges without overflow

An arm64 syzkaller reproducer creates a FUSE character device with
major:minor 1:1, so opening it uses the /dev/mem file operations. It
maps one page from offset 0xfffffffffffff000 at user address zero.
The next openat() with a NULL pathname triggers a synchronous external
abort (SEA, ESR 0x96000010) in strncpy_from_user() via do_getname(),
panicking the kernel.
